title: Adapter bootstrapping and deterministic pinning for embedding + pairwise reranker with published performance profile
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: We need a repeatable, auditable pipeline to bring new embedding + pairwise-reranker model pairs into the Redwood catalog, pin a deterministic serving variant for customers, and publish a machine-readable performance profile for Console and Optimize. Current onboarding steps are ad-hoc: artifacts live in multiple places, version pins are human-managed, and published profiles are incomplete for pairwise rerankers (no latency/throughput envelope).

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic adapter that converts model artifacts into a deployable serving variant and profile metadata.
- Establish a semantic versioning + build hash scheme for model artifacts and pins that is machine-readable (e.g., v1.2.0+build.20260305).
- Automate profile extraction (quality + perf) and publish to the catalog with provenance links.
- Support a safe canary rollout path for replacing pinned variants.

Success metrics (initial targets):
- Ingestion automation: onboarding time <= 2 hours (from artifact push to profile publish) for standard models.
- Quality gates: pairwise reranker MRR >= 0.60 on Redwood eval set; embedding recall@10 >= 0.83 (on v0 eval datasets).
- Latency targets: embedding P95 <= 40ms (CPU-optimized batch), reranker P95 <= 140ms (single-request on dedicated GPU). Throughput envelope published.
- Catalog: new model entry with profile, artifact URI, and pin metadata appears in Console within 30 minutes of publish.

Design decisions and constraints:
1) Artifact flow: model artifact (storage URI) -> adapter job (containerized) -> artifact registry entry (artifact://catalog/<name>:<semver+build>) -> profile builder job executes standardized eval harness -> profile JSON published to catalog service. All artifacts include a provenance block with PR/commit/CI-run links.
2) Pinning policy: major version pins are explicit and require PM approval; minor/patch may be auto-promoted after passing staged canary and a 24-hour observability window. Pin metadata contains: pinned_variant_id, semver, build_hash, created_by, approved_by.
3) Profile schema: extend current profile to include reranker-specific metrics (MRR, MAP, recall@k per k=1,5,10), embedding similarity distributions, kv-cache memory footprint, quantization profile used, and perf envelope (p50/p95/p99 latency for representative batch sizes). Schema will be backward compatible.
4) Canary rollout: support 5% traffic canary in Dedicated and Hosted with automatic rollback on these triggers: quality regression > 2% absolute on monitored eval prompts OR latency p95 increase > 30% vs baseline OR error rate > 0.5% absolute.
5) Security/data: adapter runs in restricted VPC slot; models that touch private datasets require security sign-off and KMS key reference in metadata.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Step 1: Adapter container and registry integration (ENG work) — build adapter that normalizes checkpoints and emits artifact metadata. (owner: Miguel)
- Step 2: Profile builder harness — standardized eval runner that takes artifact and outputs profile JSON and plots. (owner: Jamie Li)
- Step 3: Catalog publish API — extend service to accept new profile fields and provenance. (owner: Aisha)
- Step 4: Pin store changes — add pin metadata and automated canary operator. (owner: Infra)
- Step 5: Console display + Optimize hooks — surface new metrics and allow pin management. (owner: Console PM)

Testing plan / QA:
- Unit tests for adapter transformations and semantic version parser.
- End-to-end staging job: run sample model (public open model) through adapter -> profile builder -> publish to staging catalog; verify Console entry and dashboard links.
- Performance regression tests using the performance lab; record p50/p95 across GPU types.
- Security review for artifacts with private datasets.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adapter produces artifact entries with semver+build hash and provenance fields.
- Profile JSON conforms to new schema and contains reranker metrics and perf envelope.
- Catalog API accepts and persists the profile; Console shows the model entry and profile artifacts.
- Canary rollout path configurable and triggered from Console with automatic rollback rules enforced.
- Documentation page created with onboarding checklist and troubleshooting tips.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Eval harnesses are non-deterministic and produce noisy quality metrics. Mitigation: publish sample size and confidence intervals; require multiple runs before auto-promotion.
- Risk: New profile schema breaks older Console consumers. Mitigation: add schema version and fallback display.
